evals.prompt: Make me an Atari 2600 Pong game in batari Basic. Left paddle = player0 controlled by joystick up/down. Right paddle = player1 controlled by simple AI that follows the ball. The ball bounces off the top and bottom edges and off both paddles; a point is scored when the ball passes a paddle; the score shows at the bottom of the screen; after a point the ball serves again from the center. Compile it with 2600bas and iterate until it compiles cleanly. Save the final game as pong.bas (plus its pong.bas.bin).
evals.expected_output: pong.bas that compiles to a valid 4K ROM, with joystick-controlled left paddle, AI right paddle, bouncing ball, scoring, and serve reset
expectations: pong.bas exists in the outputs directory
The submitted pong.bas compiles cleanly: 2600bas prints 'Complete. (0)' and produces a ROM
A .bas.bin ROM is produced whose size is a power of 2 (at least 4096 bytes)
Left paddle is moved by joystick up/down (joy0up/joy0down affect player0y)
Ball bounces off the top and bottom of the screen (ball y compared against screen limits and direction reverses)
Right paddle AI: player1y moves toward the ball's y position
Score increases when the ball passes a paddle
Ball is reset toward the screen center after a point
No invalid bB syntax remains (no endif keyword, no == operator, no colon-terminated labels)

evals.prompt: Write a small batari Basic game for the Atari 2600: a maze drawn with the playfield. The player sprite moves through the maze with the joystick and cannot pass through playfield walls. Scattered in the maze are items (drawn as playfield pixels); when the player touches an item it disappears and the score goes up by 100. When all items are collected the screen flashes and shows a win state until the game is reset. Compile with 2600bas and fix all errors until it builds. Save the final game as maze.bas (plus its maze.bas.bin).
evals.expected_output: maze.bas that compiles to a valid ROM, with playfield maze, wall collision blocking movement, collectible playfield items worth 100, and a win-flash state
expectations: maze.bas exists in the outputs directory
The submitted maze.bas compiles cleanly: 2600bas prints 'Complete. (0)' and produces a ROM
A .bas.bin ROM is produced whose size is a power of 2 (at least 4096 bytes)
A playfield: block defines visible maze walls
The player cannot pass through walls: collision(player0,playfield) is checked (and the move is undone or blocked)
Player moves with the joystick (joy0left/right/up/down all handled)
Items are playfield pixels removed when collected (pfpixel ... off or equivalent)
Score increases by 100 per item collected
A win state exists when all items are collected (flag/counter + flashing screen or visual change, looping until reset)

evals.prompt: Write a batari Basic Atari 2600 game: first a title screen that says SHOOTER (rough letters are fine), then the game: you move a ship along the bottom of the screen with the joystick and press fire to shoot a missile upward at descending alien sprites. Shooting an alien plays a sound effect and adds 50 to the score. Aliens respawn at the top and get faster as the score grows. It is game over when an alien reaches the bottom; the game restarts when the reset switch is pressed. Compile with 2600bas, fixing errors until it builds cleanly. Save the final game as shooter.bas (plus its shooter.bas.bin).
evals.expected_output: shooter.bas that compiles to a valid ROM, with title screen, ship movement, firing missiles, hit detection with sound and +50 score, accelerating aliens, game over and reset-switch restart
expectations: shooter.bas exists in the outputs directory
The submitted shooter.bas compiles cleanly: 2600bas prints 'Complete. (0)' and produces a ROM
A .bas.bin ROM is produced whose size is a power of 2 (at least 4096 bytes)
A title-screen state runs before gameplay (screen/state flag with its own drawscreen loop)
Pressing fire launches a missile from the ship (missile0 position derived from player0, missile moves upward)
Alien hits detected via collision(missile0,player1) checked after drawscreen
A sound effect plays on shoot or hit (AUDV0/AUDC0/AUDF0 are set)
Score increases by 50 when an alien is hit
Aliens descend over time and their speed increases as the score grows
Game over triggers when an alien reaches the bottom, and the game restarts on the reset switch (switchreset)

evals.prompt: Write a batari Basic Atari 2600 game called bugs.bas: a ship at the bottom that the joystick moves left and right, and four kinds of enemy that drift down the screen. Keep the enemy kind in a variable numbered 1 to 4, give each kind its own sprite shape and its own colour, and pick the shape with an on..goto. Firing destroys an enemy and scores; an enemy reaching the bottom costs a life; three lives then game over. Compile it, then actually run the ROM headless under gopher2600 and save at least three screenshots taken at different points (title, early play, later play). Confirm from the screenshots that the game is really drawing and really changing - a screenshot that is entirely one colour, or that is pixel-identical to the previous one, means the program crashed or hung and you must fix it before finishing. Save bugs.bas, bugs.bas.bin and the screenshots.
evals.expected_output: bugs.bas compiling to a valid ROM, plus screenshots from a headless run that are neither blank nor identical to each other, demonstrating the game boots, draws and responds
expectations: bugs.bas exists in the outputs directory
The submitted bugs.bas compiles cleanly: 2600bas prints 'Complete. (0)' and produces a ROM
A .bas.bin ROM is produced whose size is a power of 2 (at least 4096 bytes)
At least three screenshot .png files were produced from a headless emulator run
No screenshot is blank: in each one, the single most common pixel colour covers less than 99% of the frame
The screenshots are not all identical to one another (the game is not frozen)
An on..goto selects the enemy sprite by kind

The on..goto is safe for a 1-based variable: either index 0 is padded with a do-nothing label so a kind of 4 lands inside the label list, or the variable is decremented before the on..goto. A 1-to-4 variable indexing a bare four-label list is a defect

Every player0:/player1: graphics block is positioned where it will actually execute - in setup code before the main loop, or inside a subroutine that is called - and not stranded after the end of the main loop where control never reaches it
Any loop that counts a variable up to a limit while calling a subroutine does not use a counter that the subroutine overwrites (no infinite loop from a clobbered scratch variable)
COLUP0/COLUP1 are set inside the main loop rather than only once at startup

evals.prompt: Using the batari Basic multisprite kernel, write chase.bas: a player0 character the joystick moves freely, and four virtual sprites (player2 to player5) that are enemies moving horizontally across the screen. Each enemy should be visible at all times while it is on screen. There must also be a way to take an enemy out of play so that it is completely invisible. Compile it, run it headless and take screenshots to confirm all four enemies are actually on screen together, and that a removed enemy leaves no trace at the screen edges.
evals.expected_output: chase.bas compiling to a valid ROM, with four virtual sprites that are all simultaneously visible in a screenshot, and a removal mechanism that leaves no sliver at the screen edges
expectations: chase.bas exists in the outputs directory
The submitted chase.bas compiles cleanly and produces a ROM whose size is a power of 2 (at least 4096 bytes)
'set kernel multisprite' is used
Each of player2-player5 is given its own separated band of y values, rather than all sharing overlapping vertical positions - overlapping virtual sprites flicker and appear missing in a single frame

Taking an enemy out of play does more than set its x to 200: because x=200 wraps back onto the screen in the multisprite kernel, the sprite is also painted in the background colour (or otherwise genuinely hidden)
A screenshot from a headless run shows four distinct enemy sprites on screen at once
No screenshot is blank: the most common pixel colour covers less than 99% of the frame
Enemy colours use the multisprite per-sprite colour registers (_COLUP1, COLUP2-COLUP5) rather than expecting COLUP1 to work for virtual sprites

evals.prompt: Write a small batari Basic game called dodger.bas (a sprite the joystick moves left and right along the bottom, avoiding blocks that fall from the top; score goes up the longer you survive). Compile it, then publish it as a browser-playable page using javatari.js: put the page at games/dodger/index.html, keep the ROM in that same folder, and copy the embedded javatari.js build to a javatari/ folder at the top level so it is NOT beside the page. Verify the page really loads the ROM before you call it done - do not just assert that the path looks right. Hand back the exact command a human runs to play it.
evals.expected_output: dodger.bas compiling to a valid ROM, plus games/dodger/index.html that genuinely loads the ROM when served over HTTP, and instructions that tell the human to serve the directory rather than open the file
expectations: dodger.bas exists and compiles cleanly: 2600bas prints 'Complete. (0)' and produces a ROM whose size is a power of 2 (at least 4096 bytes)
games/dodger/index.html exists and contains an element with id="javatari-screen"
The page references javatari.js with a path that is correct relative to the page's own URL (../../javatari/javatari.js from games/dodger/), not relative to the server root
The ROM is named either via a ?ROM= parameter or via Javatari.CARTRIDGE_URL, and the value resolves relative to the page's URL to the ROM's actual location
Javatari.CARTRIDGE_URL, if used, is set in a script that comes AFTER the javatari.js script tag
The page was actually verified by loading it over http:// - a served page plus a fetched ROM, or a headless browser check - rather than only reasoned about
The instructions given to the human tell them to serve the directory over HTTP (python3 -m http.server or equivalent) and open a http://localhost URL
The instructions do NOT tell the human to open the .html file directly, double-click it, or use a file:// URL, since javatari cannot fetch the ROM over file://
A defect to catch: if the submission diagnoses a 'Could not load file / Error: 0' symptom as a wrong ROM path rather than as the file:// protocol blocking the XHR, that is wrong
